hindi: "अहो, साधु!" — प्राणियों द्वारा हर्ष से आकाश में उठाया गया यह स्निग्ध और गम्भीर घोष तीनों लोकों में गूँज उठा।
english: "Ah, well done!" — this cry, smooth and deep, raised in the sky by beings out of joy, resounded through the three worlds.
notes: bhūtaiḥ: 'beings' (could also mean spirits or elemental beings). anvavādayat: literally 'caused to sound along/after', i.e. made the worlds echo.

hindi: शुभ वायु बहने लगी, सभी दिशाएँ प्रकाश से खिल उठीं, और जल से युक्त दिव्य पुष्प-वर्षाएँ भी हुईं।
english: An auspicious wind blew, all the directions shone open with radiance, and heavenly showers of flowers, together with water, fell.
notes: sajalāḥ: 'with water', i.e. the flower showers came with drops of water (or with rain).

hindi: तब ज्ञान की देवियाँ — बुद्धि, सिद्धि, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति, कीर्ति, क्षमा और दया — अग्निवेश आदि में प्रविष्ट हुईं।
english: Then the deities of knowledge — Intellect (buddhi), Accomplishment (siddhi), Memory (smṛti), Retention (medhā), Steadfastness (dhṛti), Fame (kīrti), Forbearance (kṣamā) and Compassion (dayā) — entered Agniveśa and the others headed by him.
notes: kṣamādayā is printed as one token; it is two nominatives kṣamā and dayā written together (no sandhi change). A reading kṣamā-ādayaḥ 'forbearance and the rest' would need a different text.

hindi: और इनके वे तन्त्र-ग्रन्थ परम ऋषियों द्वारा अनुमोदित होकर प्राणि-समूहों के कल्याण के लिए पृथ्वी पर प्रतिष्ठित हुए।
english: And those treatises (tantra) of theirs, approved by the supreme sages, gained an established place on earth for the welfare of the multitudes of beings.
notes: eṣām 'of these' refers to Agniveśa and his fellow pupils of the preceding verses. bhava: 'welfare, well-being' (also 'existence').

hindi: जिसमें हितकर और अहितकर, सुखी और दुःखी आयु, उस आयु के लिए हित और अहित, उसका मान तथा स्वयं वह आयु बताई गई है, वह आयुर्वेद कहलाता है।
english: That in which wholesome and unwholesome life, happy and unhappy life, what is wholesome and unwholesome for it, its measure, and life itself are described, is called Āyurveda (the science of life).

text_flags.why: the word for 'unhappy/sorrow' is duḥkha; the visarga is missing; likely typo (sense requires duḥkha, the opposite of sukha)

notes: Usual reading: four kinds of life (hita, ahita, sukha, duḥkha āyus); tasya hitāhitam = what is good and bad for life; mānam = its measure (length); tat = life itself.

words.gloss: union of body, senses, mind and self
words.gram: m. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शरीर, इन्द्रिय, सत्त्व अर्थात् मन और आत्मा का संयोग आयु है; धारि, जीवित, नित्यग और अनुबन्ध — इन पर्यायों से आयु कही जाती है।
english: The union of body, senses, mind (sattva) and self (ātman) is life (āyus); it is called by the synonyms dhāri (sustaining), jīvita (living), nityaga (ever-moving) and anubandha (continuity).
notes: āyuḥ in 42b is the predicate of the whole verse: the union is āyus, and dhāri, jīvita, nityaga, anubandha are its synonyms.

words.gloss: of the knowers of the Vedas

hindi: आयु का वह वेद, जिसे वेदज्ञ सबसे पुण्यमय मानते हैं और जो मनुष्यों के लिए दोनों लोकों में हितकर है, आगे कहा जाएगा।
english: The science (veda) of that life, regarded by the knowers of the Vedas as the most sacred, which is beneficial to humans in both worlds, will be taught.
notes: yat (n.) refers to vedaḥ (m.) by sense, or means 'what is beneficial'. lokayor ubhayoḥ: 'this world and the next'; the dual could also be genitive. vakṣyate is a middle future used passively.

hindi: सब पदार्थों की वृद्धि का कारण सदा सामान्य है और ह्रास का कारण विशेष है; प्रवृत्ति तो दोनों की होती है।
english: Sameness (sāmānya) is always the cause of increase of all entities, and difference (viśeṣa) the cause of decrease; but application belongs to both.
notes: pravṛttir ubhayasya tu is read in different ways: both are applied (in treatment), or both operate together on things. Kept literal.

hindi: सामान्य एकत्व करने वाला है और विशेष पृथक्त्व करने वाला; तुल्यार्थता ही सामान्य है और विशेष उसका विपरीत है।
english: Sāmānya produces oneness, while viśeṣa produces separateness; sāmānya is indeed likeness of things, and viśeṣa is the opposite.

hindi: सत्त्व अर्थात् मन, आत्मा और शरीर — यह त्रय त्रिदण्ड के समान है; इनके संयोग से लोक टिका रहता है, और उसी में सब प्रतिष्ठित है।
english: Mind (sattva), self and body — this triad is like a tripod; by their union the world (of living beings) stands, and in it everything is established.
notes: tridaṇḍa: three staffs tied together that stand only jointly. loka is taken by commentators as the living person; tatra may refer to that union.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś

hindi: वही पुरुष है, वही चेतन है, और वही इस वेद का अधिकरण अर्थात् विषय माना गया है; उसी के लिए यह वेद प्रकाशित किया गया है।
english: That (union) is the person (pumān); it is sentient; and it is declared the subject matter of this science; for its sake this science has been revealed.
notes: saḥ (m.) agrees with pumān; the following tat (n.) refers to the union (saṃyoga) of the previous verse.

hindi: आकाश आदि, आत्मा, मन, काल और दिशाएँ — यह द्रव्यों का संग्रह है; इन्द्रियों से युक्त द्रव्य चेतन है और इन्द्रियरहित द्रव्य अचेतन।
english: Ether and the others, the self, mind, time and the directions — this is the group of substances (dravya). A substance with senses is sentient; one without senses is insentient.
notes: khādīni: the five elements beginning with kha (ether).

hindi: शब्द आदि अर्थों सहित गुरु आदि, बुद्धि, तथा प्रयत्न तक के पर आदि — ये गुण कहे गए हैं; प्रयत्न-पूर्वक होने वाली चेष्टा कर्म कहलाती है।
english: The qualities (guṇa) are declared to be: the sense objects (artha), together with heaviness and the rest (guru etc.), intellect (buddhi), and para and the rest ending with effort (prayatna). Movement preceded by effort is called action (karma).
notes: sārthāḥ: with the arthas (sound, touch, form, taste, smell). parādayaḥ prayatnāntāḥ: the list para, apara, yukti, saṃkhyā, saṃyoga, vibhāga, pṛthaktva, parimāṇa, saṃskāra, abhyāsa, given later in the text (Sūtrasthāna 26), ending with prayatna. prayatnādi karma may also be read 'action begins with effort'.

hindi: पृथ्वी आदि का गुणों के साथ अपृथग्भाव समवाय माना गया है; वह नित्य है, क्योंकि जहाँ द्रव्य है वहाँ गुण अनियत नहीं होता।
english: Inherence (samavāya) is held to be the inseparable existence of earth and the other substances with their qualities; it is eternal, for where there is a substance, quality is not unfixed there.

hindi: जिसमें कर्म और गुण आश्रित रहते हैं और जो समवायी कारण है, वह द्रव्य है; गुण तो समवायी, निश्चेष्ट कारण है।
english: That in which actions and qualities reside and which is the inherent (samavāyin) cause is substance (dravya); quality (guṇa), however, is an inherent but motionless cause.

words.gloss: of what is to be done

hindi: जो द्रव्य में आश्रित रहकर संयोग और विभाग का कारण है और करने योग्य की क्रिया है, वह कर्म है; कर्म किसी अन्य की अपेक्षा नहीं करता।
english: That which, residing in a substance, is the cause of conjunction and disjunction, and is the activity of what is to be done, is action (karma); action depends on nothing else.
notes: Usual reading: karma needs nothing else to cause conjunction and disjunction. dravyam āśritam: 'resting on a substance' (dravyam as object of āśrita).

words.gloss: effect, what is to be achieved
bringing about equilibrium of the dhātus

hindi: इस प्रकार कारण कहा गया। यहाँ धातुओं की समता को कार्य कहा जाता है, और धातु-साम्य की क्रिया इस तन्त्र का प्रयोजन कही गई है।
english: Thus the cause has been stated. Here the effect (kārya) is said to be the equilibrium of the dhātus, and the act of bringing about that equilibrium is declared the purpose of this treatise.

words.gloss: of time, intellect and sense objects

hindi: काल, बुद्धि और इन्द्रियार्थों का मिथ्या योग, अयोग और अतियोग — यह दो आश्रयों वाले रोगों के कारणों का तीन प्रकार का संग्रह है।
english: Wrong, deficient (non-) and excessive conjunction of time, intellect and sense objects — this is the threefold summary of the causes of diseases, which have two seats.
notes: yogo mithyā na cāti ca = mithyāyoga, ayoga, atiyoga. indriyārtha read as 'sense objects' (it could also be split indriya + artha, senses and their objects). The two seats are body and mind (next verse).

hindi: शरीर और सत्त्व नामक मन रोगों के आश्रय माने गए हैं, और वैसे ही सुखों के भी; सुखों का कारण तो सम योग है।
english: The body and that which is called sattva (the mind) are held to be the seat of diseases, and likewise of well-being (sukha); the cause of well-being is balanced conjunction.
notes: sukha here is commonly taken as health (the opposite of vyādhi). samaḥ yogaḥ = samayoga, proper conjunction of time, intellect and sense objects.

words.gloss: with mind, qualities of the elements and senses

hindi: आत्मा तो निर्विकार और पर है; वह सत्त्व, भूतों के गुणों और इन्द्रियों के साथ मिलकर चैतन्य का कारण है; वह नित्य और द्रष्टा है, क्योंकि वह क्रियाओं को देखता है।
english: The self, however, is changeless and supreme; together with the mind, the qualities of the elements and the senses, it is the cause of consciousness; it is eternal and the seer, for it sees actions.
notes: sattvabhūtaguṇendriyaiḥ: bhūtaguṇa may be 'qualities of the elements' or 'elements and qualities' taken separately. The instrumental is taken as 'together with'.

hindi: वायु, पित्त और कफ — यह शारीरिक दोषों का संग्रह कहा गया है; और मानस दोष रज और तम बताए गए हैं।
english: Vāyu (Vāta), Pitta and Kapha are stated to be the group of bodily doṣas; the mental group, on the other hand, is indicated as Rajas and Tamas.

words.gloss: based on the divine and on reasoning
by knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory and concentration

hindi: पहला अर्थात् शारीरिक दोष-समूह दैवव्यपाश्रय और युक्तिव्यपाश्रय औषधों से शान्त होता है; मानस दोष ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति और समाधि से।
english: The former (the bodily group) is pacified by remedies based on the divine (daiva-vyapāśraya) and on reasoning (yukti-vyapāśraya); the mental group by knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory and concentration (samādhi).

hindi: वात रूक्ष, शीत, लघु, सूक्ष्म, चल, विशद और खर है; वह विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से शान्त होता है।
english: Vāta (māruta, wind) is dry, cold, light, subtle, mobile, non-slimy (viśada) and rough; it is pacified by substances with opposite qualities.
notes: The adjectives of 59a agree with mārutaḥ in 59b.

hindi: पित्त थोड़ी स्निग्धता वाला, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, द्रव, अम्ल, सर और कटु है; वह विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से शीघ्र शान्त होता है।
english: Pitta is slightly unctuous, hot, sharp, liquid, sour, flowing (sara) and pungent; it is quickly pacified by substances with opposite qualities.
notes: sasneha: literally 'with unctuousness'; commentators take it as 'slightly unctuous'.

words.gloss: heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable, slimy

hindi: कफ के गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, मधुर, स्थिर और पिच्छिल गुण विपरीत गुणों से शान्त होते हैं।
english: The qualities of Kapha (śleṣman) — heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable and slimy — are pacified by opposite qualities.

words.gloss: administered with regard to place, dose and time

hindi: विपरीत गुणों वाली और देश, मात्रा तथा काल के अनुसार प्रयुक्त औषधियों से साध्य माने गए विकार दूर हो जाते हैं।
english: Disorders regarded as curable are reversed by medicines of opposite qualities, administered with due regard to place, dose and time.

hindi: परन्तु असाध्य रोगों की चिकित्सा का उपदेश नहीं किया जाता। इसके आगे प्रत्येक द्रव्य के अनुसार गुण और कर्म बताए जाएँगे।
english: But treatment of incurable diseases is not taught. Further, from here on, the qualities and actions will be stated substance by substance.
notes: guṇakarmāṇi (pl.) with singular vakṣyate is a loose agreement; some editions read guṇakarma ca vakṣyate. Not changed.

hindi: रसना इन्द्रिय का विषय रस है; उसका द्रव्य जल और पृथ्वी हैं; उसकी उत्पत्ति और विशेषता में आकाश आदि तीन कारण हैं।
english: Taste (rasa) is the object of the tongue; its substratum is water and also earth; in its formation and its differentiation the three beginning with ether are the causes.
notes: The three beginning with kha are ether, air and fire. Commentators differ on whether nirvṛtti also involves water and earth.

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल, लवण, कटु, तिक्त और कषाय — रसों का यह छह का संग्रह कहा गया है।
english: Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent — this set of six is held to be the summary of the tastes (rasa).

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रस वायु को; कषाय, मधुर और तिक्त रस पित्त को; तथा कषाय, कटु और तिक्त रस कफ को जीतते हैं।
english: Sweet, sour and salty tastes overcome Vāyu (Vāta); astringent, sweet and bitter overcome Pitta; astringent, pungent and bitter overcome Kapha.

hindi: कुछ द्रव्य दोषों को शान्त करने वाले हैं, कुछ धातुओं को दूषित करने वाले, और कुछ स्वस्थवृत्त में उपयोगी माने गए हैं — इस प्रकार द्रव्य तीन प्रकार का कहा जाता है।
english: Some substances pacify the doṣas, some vitiate the dhātus, and some are approved for maintaining health — thus substance (dravya) is said to be threefold.

hindi: वह द्रव्य फिर तीन प्रकार का कहा गया है — जांगम, औद्भिद और पार्थिव। मधु, गोरस, पित्त, वसा, मज्जा, रक्त, मांस,
english: That (substance) again is declared threefold: animal (jaṅgama), plant-born (audbhida) and earthly (pārthiva). Honeys, cow products, bile, fat, marrow, blood, flesh,
notes: The list of animal products in 68b continues into 69, which ends 'are used from animals'; the edition's grouping is kept. madhūni: plural, the kinds of honey. pitta here is animal bile, not the doṣa.

words.gloss: faeces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails

hindi: मल, मूत्र, चर्म, वीर्य, अस्थि, स्नायु, सींग, नख, खुर, केश, रोम और गोरोचन — ये जांगम द्रव्यों से लेकर प्रयोग में लाए जाते हैं।
english: faeces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails, hooves, head hair, body hair and rocanā are the things used from animals.
notes: Continues the list begun in 68b. retosthi = retas + asthi inside the compound (printed without avagraha). rocanā: standard identification gorocanā, a gallstone (bezoar) of cattle.

hindi: सोना, मल सहित पाँच धातुएँ, बालू, सुधा अर्थात् चूना, मैनसिल और हरताल, मणियाँ, लवण, गेरू और अञ्जन —
english: Gold, the five metals (loha) with their dross (mala), along with sand, lime (sudhā), realgar (manaḥśilā) and orpiment (āla), gems, salt, red ochre (gairika) and añjana (collyrium mineral) —
notes: The sentence ends in 71a ('are indicated as earthly medicine'). sasikatāḥ may qualify lohāḥ ('together with sand') or simply add sand (sikatā) to the list. The five metals are not named here; commentators usually give copper, silver, tin, lead and iron (disputed). manaḥśilā = realgar (standard); āla = haritāla, orpiment (standard); gairika = red ochre (standard); añjana = stibnite/antimony sulphide (probable; galena also proposed, disputed).

hindi: ये पार्थिव औषध बताए गए हैं। औद्भिद औषध तो चार प्रकार का है — वनस्पति, वीरुध्, वानस्पत्य और ओषधि।
english: — are indicated as earthly medicine. The plant-born, however, is fourfold: vanaspati, vīrudh, vānaspatya and oṣadhi.
notes: 71a completes the list of 70. The four plant classes are defined in 72.

words.gloss: ending with the ripening of fruit

hindi: वनस्पति फलों से, वानस्पत्य फूलों और फलों से पहचाने जाते हैं; ओषधियाँ वे हैं जिनका अन्त फल पकने पर होता है, और वीरुध् फैलने वाली बेलों से पहचाने गए हैं।
english: Vanaspati is known by its fruits, vānaspatya by flowers and also fruits; oṣadhis are those whose life ends with the ripening of their fruit; and vīrudhs are known by their spreading runners.
notes: Commentators take vanaspati as a tree bearing fruit without evident flowers (e.g. figs) and vānaspatya as one with both flowers and fruit. The text itself only says 'by fruits', 'by flowers and fruits'.
